classification.difficultyReason: Construct a speed–time graph with three prescribed regimes and an area of 100 m, then distinguish the speed gained under constant acceleration from the absolute speed.

content.prompt: A sprinter runs 100 metres in 10 seconds. Their instantaneous speed increases steadily for the first 4 seconds, remains constant for 3 seconds, and then decreases for the final 3 seconds.

answer.short: One possible graph rises to $t=4\text{ s}$, stays level to $t=7\text{ s}$ and falls to $t=10\text{ s}$. The area under it is $100\text{ m}$.
answer.worked:
For this sketch, choose zero speed at the start and finish. Let the speed on the horizontal section be $V$ metres per second. The two triangles and the rectangle give the total distance.

$$\begin{align*}100&=\tfrac12(4)V+3V+\tfrac12(3)V\\100&=\tfrac{13}{2}V\\V&=\tfrac{200}{13}\end{align*}$$

Draw straight segments through $(0,0)$, $(4,\frac{200}{13})$, $(7,\frac{200}{13})$ and $(10,0)$.

spec.description: Authored speed–time graph for the requested sketch, with straight rising, level and falling segments.
spec.mathematics: Vertices are (0,0), (4,200/13), (7,200/13) and (10,0). The enclosed area above the time axis is 100 metres.

children.prompt: The average speed over the race.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: The change in speed from the start to $t=3\text{ s}$ if the acceleration is constant at $2.5\text{ m/s}^2$ during the first 4 seconds. Can you determine the instantaneous speed at $t=3\text{ s}$? Explain.

answer.short: $v(3)=v(0)+7.5\text{ m/s}$. A numerical speed requires the sprinter’s initial speed.
answer.worked:
The constant acceleration adds $2.5\text{ m/s}$ to the speed each second during the first four seconds.

$$\begin{align*}v(3)&=v(0)+(2.5\text{ m/s}^2)(3\text{ s})\\v(3)&=v(0)+7.5\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$$

The initial speed is unspecified. A start from rest would give a speed of $10\text{ m/s}$ at four seconds. The sprinter would then cover $20\text{ m}$ in the first four seconds, $30\text{ m}$ in the next three and less than $30\text{ m}$ in the final three. That would give a race distance below $80\text{ m}$.
